newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end mixed after zigzagging on Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end mixed after zigzagging on Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended a three-day rally to close mixed Tuesday after see-saw trading amid fallout from volatile U.S. markets.
Traders and analysts also cited light profit taking.

"The bourse was volatile due to skittishness on international markets ahead of U.S. inflation data, which makes the market nervous here, also," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 0.65 point, or 0.02 percent, at 3,930.74.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 18.54 at 7,274.21 points, with the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond down 14/32 to yield 6.92 percent when the bourse was closing.

"U.S. producer and consumer prices tomorrow and Thursday could give a closer idea of what the FOMC will do on May 20," Rojas added, referring to the Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rate policy.
"Also, we saw some dealers take advantage for much of the day of a forecast rise in Cetes rates to take profits after a three-day rally," Rojas said.

A Reuter survey of nine money market dealers showed they predicted on average Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 19.37 percent. This would be an increase of 76 basis points since last week's auction.

Dealers said the bourse had previously climbed as high as 3,954.03, just shy of a February 25 record of 3,960.06, on foreign buyers encouraged by the Dow Jones notching up a new trading high of 7,315.83 points.
Trading volume of 121.2 million shares was much brisker than for many recent sessions due to the presence of foreign investors.
Traders said although the IPC edged ahead, blue chips as a whole were mixed, with decliners outpacing gainers by 20 to 10, and five unchanged.
Telecomms firm Telmex and financial stock Bancomer weighed most on the downside. The two stocks together accounted for one fifth of all shares traded.
"They took profits on Telmex and Bancomer. Telmex ADRs had trouble breaking resistance at 44," a desk trader said.
Telmex L shares ended down 10 centavos at 17.24 pesos, while its ADRs closed off 1/4 at 43-1/2.
Retail chain Cifra and holding company Accelsa were the most heavily traded market gains.
"Accelsa's performance has drawn some attention because of the volume it has accumulated," a trader said.
Traders said Cifra had gained on speculation of forthcoming increased stake by Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
Accelsa gained eight centavos to 2.15 pesos, while Cifra also ended up eight centavos, at 12.68 pesos.
Troubled holding company Grupo Sidek and its tourist arm Situr ended topped the prominent gainers' list.
"Sidek gained on thin volume. They are still speculating over a financial restructuring deal, but there is nothing new," a trader said.
Sidek gained nine centavos to 62 centavos, while Situr closed up six centavos at 48 centavos.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
